AccountReconcile.description:
The real balance of an account (what the bank says), to match the app to it.

Same sign as `balance_minor`: on a credit card, negative = you owe. The app registers an
adjustment for the difference, or nothing if there is none. Zero is a valid balance.
AccountReconcile.title: AccountReconcile

AccountRef.description: An account as a movement shows it (archived ones too).
AccountRef.title: AccountRef

AccountUpdate.description: Fields to change: only the ones sent are updated. The type of an account cannot change.
AccountUpdate.title: AccountUpdate

AccountWithBalance.description:
What the API returns for an account: the account plus its balance.

`AccountRead` has no balance because `accounts` cannot ask `transactions` for it (the module
order): the router composes the two. `balance_minor` is the sum of the confirmed, not deleted
entries, with its sign, in the minor unit of the currency of the space. On a credit card it is
negative when you owe (the debt is its opposite).
AccountWithBalance.title: AccountWithBalance

BalanceSummaryRead.description:
The balances of the space, in the minor unit of its currency.

Only confirmed, not deleted movements count. `card_debt_minor` is positive when the cards are
owed (and negative if a card is paid in excess: it is not clamped, so the net always adds up).
BalanceSummaryRead.title: BalanceSummaryRead

CategoryCreate.description:
A principal category, or a subcategory when `parent_id` is sent.

A subcategory must have the kind of its principal category, which cannot itself be a
subcategory. Those rules depend on stored data, so the service checks them.
CategoryCreate.title: CategoryCreate

CategoryRef.description: A category as a movement shows it; `parent` is the main category of a subcategory.
CategoryRef.title: CategoryRef

CategoryUpdate.description: Fields to change: only the ones sent are updated. The kind and the parent never change.
CategoryUpdate.title: CategoryUpdate

ErrorResponse.description: Body of every error response except 422, for `responses={404: {"model": ErrorResponse}}`.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

ExpenseCreate.description: Money goes out of an account, classified in an expense category (or its subcategory).
ExpenseCreate.title: ExpenseCreate

IncomeCreate.description: Money comes into an account, classified in an income category (or its subcategory).
IncomeCreate.title: IncomeCreate

MovementListItem.description:
An item of the list. `balance_after_minor` appears only when the list is filtered by account.

It is the balance of that account right after this movement, with the sign of `balance_minor`
(on a credit card, negative = you owe), whatever the other filters are: a movement that the
filters hide still counts. It is null for a movement that does not count for a balance
(pending or skipped) and always when there is no `account_id` filter.
MovementListItem.title: MovementListItem

MovementRead.description:
A movement as the list and the detail show it, in the minor unit of the space's currency.

`amount_minor` has a sign by type: an expense is negative, an income positive, an adjustment
carries its own sign (the change of the balance) and a transfer is the unsigned amount that
moved (to know whether it came in or went out of an account, compare `from_account` and
`to_account` with it). The accounts depend on the type: an expense, an income and an
adjustment have `account`; a transfer has `from_account` and `to_account`. Only an expense
and an income have `category`.
MovementRead.title: MovementRead

SpaceRead.description:
What the API answers: the space and whether its currency can still be changed.

`currency_locked` is true once the space has any transaction (pending, skipped or deleted
included): from then on `PATCH /spaces/{id}` refuses a different currency with a 409. It is
the same rule, asked the same way (`transactions.service.space_has_transactions`).
SpaceRead.title: SpaceRead

SpaceUpdate.description: Fields to change: only the ones sent are updated. Only the currency can be changed so far.
SpaceUpdate.title: SpaceUpdate

TransactionSummaryRead.description:
What the filtered period adds up to, in the minor unit of the space's currency.

`income_minor` and `expense_minor` add up only the confirmed incomes and expenses (never
adjustments, transfers, pending, skipped or deleted ones), both as positive amounts, and
`remaining_minor` is their difference ("te quedan"). The filters apply as they do to the list,
`type` included. `count` is every movement the list would show for those filters (any type and
status, deleted ones excluded): the `m` of "showing n of m".
TransactionSummaryRead.title: TransactionSummaryRead

TransferCreate.description: Money moves between two accounts of the space. Paying a card is a transfer.
TransferCreate.title: TransferCreate

delete.description:
Log out everywhere: revoke the user's sessions in Firebase and clear the cookie.

Every device of the user is logged out, not only this one. Always 204, even if there was no
session, the cookie was not valid or Firebase could not be reached (that failure is logged as
an error): the cookie is cleared in every case, so logging out never leaves the user stuck.

post.description:
Exchange a Firebase ID token (signed in less than 5 minutes ago) for the session cookie.

The cookie is HttpOnly and lasts 14 days. The first login also creates the user and their
personal space "Mi espacio" (UYU, in the given timezone) with its default categories.

get.description: The supported currencies by code, each with its ISO 4217 exponent (the minor unit).
Liveness probe: no database or external dependencies.
The spaces where the user is a member.
A space the user belongs to, with its currency and ISO 4217 exponent.

patch.description:
Change the currency of the space (409 `space_has_transactions` once it has movements).

Only while the space has no transactions, deleted ones included; the same currency it already
has changes nothing. `currency_locked` in the answer tells whether it can still be changed.

get.description: The accounts of the space by name, each with its balance. Archived ones only on request.

schema.title: Response List Accounts Spaces  Space Id  Accounts Get

post.description:
Create a bank, cash or credit card account (the cards need closing and due days).

With `initial_balance_minor` (other than 0) the account is born with that balance: an
adjustment, neither income nor expense, written in the same transaction. On a credit card it is
the current debt, negative. If the adjustment fails, the account is not created.

get.description: One account of the space with its balance, archived or not.

patch.description: Rename an account or change the days of a card. The type cannot be changed.

post.description:
Archive an account whose balance is zero (409 `account_has_balance` otherwise).

It stops showing in the list and in the selectors; its old movements stay. Archiving an
archived account changes nothing.

Match the balance of the account to the real one (what the bank says).

An adjustment (neither income nor expense) for the difference is registered; if there is none,
nothing is. `balance_minor` has the sign of the balance of the account: on a credit card,
negative = you owe. An archived account cannot be reconciled (409).
Make an archived account active again, whatever its balance (an active one: no change).

get.description: Available (bank and cash), card debt and net of the space, in its currency's minor unit.

The categories of the space, principal and sub, flat, in creation order.

The archived ones only with `include_archived`. A subcategory points at its principal with
`parent_id`.

schema.title: Response List Categories Spaces  Space Id  Categories Get

post.description:
Create a principal category, or a subcategory when `parent_id` is sent.

A subcategory has the kind of its principal category, which must be active and cannot be a
subcategory itself (422). The name must be new among its siblings, archived ones included
(409).

patch.description: Rename a category or change its icon. The kind and the parent cannot be changed.

post.description:
Archive a category, and with it the active subcategories of a principal one.

It is no longer offered for new movements; the old ones keep it. Archiving an archived
category changes nothing.

Make a category active again, and the subcategories that were archived with a principal one.

A subcategory whose principal category is archived cannot be unarchived (409).

get.description:
The movements of the space, newest first, one page at a time (cursor).

Order: `date` descending, then `id` descending. `next_cursor` is opaque: send it back as
`cursor` (with the same filters) for the next page; it is null on the last one. `limit` is 1
to 100 (50 by default). Filters, all optional and combined: `month` (`YYYY-MM`, on the local
date), `type`, `account_id`, `category_id` (a main category includes its subcategories) and
`q` (the description, ignoring case and accents). An account or category that does not exist
or is of another space matches nothing. Deleted movements are never listed; pending and
skipped ones are, with their `status`.

Amounts are in the minor unit of the currency of the space. `amount_minor` is negative for an
expense, positive for an income, signed for an adjustment and unsigned for a transfer. With
`account_id`, each item also has `balance_after_minor`, the balance of that account right
after it (negative = debt on a credit card).

post.description:
Register an expense, an income or a transfer; the backend builds the entries.

The body depends on `type`. An expense and an income take an account, a category of their kind
and a positive amount; a transfer takes two different accounts (paying a card is a transfer)
and a positive amount. `amount_minor` is always positive, in the minor unit of the currency of
the space: the backend applies the sign (on a credit card an expense raises the debt and a
transfer from a bank lowers it). The movement is born `confirmed`.

Accounts and categories must belong to the space and be active, or a 422 names the field
(`loc` is `["body", "<type>", "<field>"]`): an id of another space answers like one that does
not exist.

With the optional `Idempotency-Key` header the request can be repeated safely: the same key
(same user and space) with the same body creates nothing and answers 201 with the same
movement; with another body it is a 409 `idempotency_key_reused`. The header must be a UUID
(422 on the header otherwise).

parameters.description: A UUID the client generates for each attempt to register a movement, and reuses when it retries the same request (a double tap, a lost response). With the same key, user and space, a repeated request creates nothing and answers 201 with the same movement; the same key with another body is a 409 `idempotency_key_reused`. A key counts for 24 hours. A request that fails (4xx or 5xx) does not use the key.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: A UUID the client generates for each attempt to register a movement, and reuses when it retries the same request (a double tap, a lost response). With the same key, user and space, a repeated request creates nothing and answers 201 with the same movement; the same key with another body is a 409 `idempotency_key_reused`. A key counts for 24 hours. A request that fails (4xx or 5xx) does not use the key.
schema.title: Idempotency-Key

get.description:
Income, expense, what is left and the number of movements of the filtered period.

The same filters as the list (without `limit` nor `cursor`), `type` included. Only confirmed
incomes and expenses add up; adjustments and transfers do not. `count` is the number of
movements the list shows for those filters, for "showing n of m".

One movement of the space, with the same shape as an item of the list.

A deleted one, one of another space and one that does not exist are the same 404.
